display_name: The 2023 Merger Guidelines of the U.S. Department of Justice and Federal Trade Commission: Guideline 1's structural presumption, the frameworks of Guidelines 2 to 11, the section 3 rebuttals and the section 4 computations (agency enforcement policy, not law)
seat: the merging firms, and anyone advising them or affected by the merger, asking what the Agencies will presume, examine or credit; the Agencies are never the seat
scope: What the Agencies presume, infer, examine, credit or accept under the 2023 Merger Guidelines, never whether a merger is lawful: the Guidelines 'create no independent rights or obligations'. Encoded: Guideline 1 (HHI as the sum of squared shares on 0 to 10,000, the change in HHI, the merged firm's share, the HHI limb over 1,800 with a change over 100, the share limb over 30 percent with a change over 100, footnote 15's bands); Guidelines 2 to 6 as their stated tests, with every indicator list taken from the caller and reported, not weighed; Guidelines 7 to 10 as what each setting does to the analysis, and Guideline 11's kinds of partial ownership and effects, reported; section 3.1 failing firm (requirements A, B, C, footnote 62) and failing division (footnote 64); 3.2 entry and repositioning (footnote 65); 3.3 efficiencies (footnotes 70, 71) and footnote 31; section 4's diversion ratio, aggregate diversion ratio, value of diverted sales, upward pricing pressure indicator, footnote 72's margin, the 4.3 tools, the HMT, the SSNIP and the pipeline's implicit price, recapture, critical loss, targeting, geographic shares, market participants, and shares from a measure as Guideline 1's input. Answers NOTHING, in the readings that guard (NOTES.md section 3 lists them): Guideline 1 on shares that are negative, over 100 or do not sum to exactly 100, or on a market with no party; Guideline 4 on an HHI outside 0 to 10,000; Guideline 5 on a foreclosure share outside 0 to 100; footnote 62's test and the failing firm and division readings on a negative price or liquidation value, and when the two readings of an offer at or below liquidation value give different answers; entry on a negative time; the diversion ratios and the upward pricing pressure indicator on negative or excess units, a negative price or cost, or nothing to divide by; the SSNIP, critical loss, the HMT, geographic shares and shares on a measure on their impossible inputs. Not guarded at this commit, pending a ruling: the Guideline 3 reading, the concentration band, the presumption on the metrics and its two limbs. The number helpers (the HHI of the shares, 2ab, the value of diverted sales, footnote 72's margin, and the like) and the threshold predicates compute on whatever they are given; only the readings guard. Not encoded: the evidence discussion of section 4 (4.1, 4.2.A, 4.2.C to E, 4.3.B's framing, 4.3.D.3 to 8, 4.4's considerations), remedies, and the statutes.

forks.G1-1: the merged firm's share is the sum of the parties' pre-merger shares; the change is post minus pre (2ab for two parties)
forks.G1-2: shares must list every firm, each 0 to 100, summing to exactly 100, with at least one party; otherwise NOTHING (footnote 13's 16.67 x 6 = 100.02 is NOTHING)
forks.G1-3: 'creates or further consolidates a highly concentrated market' is a post-merger HHI over 1,800
forks.G1-4: the HHI is exact (10,000/6 for six equal firms); footnote 13's 1,667 is a rounding
forks.G1-5: footnote 15's moderately concentrated band is over 1,000 and at most 1,800
forks.G1-6: a market with one party (an acquirer from outside it) is read: the change is 0 and no presumption arises; the text, stated for 'a merger between competitors', is silent
forks.G3-1: section 1's 'highly concentrated' inference is 2.3.A's first primary factor: post-merger HHI over 1,800 and a change over 100
forks.G3-2: the inference arises from concentration or prior coordination; any primary factor allows 'may conclude', so a maverick's elimination alone gives 'may conclude' and not the inference
forks.G3-3: 'not highly concentrated' for the investigation is a post-merger HHI of at most 1,800
forks.G3-4: two inputs since the 2026-11-25 review: actual prior coordination grounds section 1's inference and 2.3.A's primary factor; failed attempts alone count only as the primary factor
forks.G4-1: concentrated means an HHI over 1,000, or a future market with few equivalent potential entrants
forks.G4-2: a reasonable probability of entering a market over 1,800 satisfies element (2) of 2.4.A unless there is substantial direct evidence of a de minimis effect; kept by the parent session's ruling of 2026-11-25 (the stated de minimis exception, and 'supplement'); the adversarial review's reading (b), leaving element (2) to the caller, is recorded as the alternative
forks.G5-1: footnote 30's share is the foreclosure share of 2.5.A.2
forks.G5-2: footnote 30 says nothing of a share of exactly 50 percent, and a named result says so
forks.G5-3: concern (C) needs the ability to limit access or visibility into rivals' information, not the incentive
forks.G6-1: dominance is the caller's finding; the text gives no share figure
forks.G8-1: Guideline 1 'collectively' treats the firms of a series as the parties to one merger, on the shares before the first acquisition
forks.G9-1: the mapping of each platform scenario to the kinds of platform competition it engages
forks.G10-1: whether a claimed benefit is in the market where competition may be lessened; nothing is weighed (result renamed 2026-11-25)
forks.FF-1: footnote 62's bar applies to any rejected offer above liquidation value, whether or not less dangerous than the merger; on FF-2's reading (b) a rejected offer at or below it bars too
forks.FF-2: an offer at or below liquidation value is computed both as not reasonable and as reasonable; the common accept or credit answer is returned, and NOTHING when the two differ
forks.FF-3: the inputs under requirements A to C are the caller's findings on the evidence the Agencies 'typically look for', and are named so (2026-11-25)
forks.FD-1: footnote 62's definition applies to a failing division, and its bar only to a rejected offer that would keep the assets in the relevant market (reading (b), taken since the 2026-11-25 review)
forks.EN-1: sufficient entry replicates one merging party on all of scale, strength and durability
forks.EN-2: entry is timely only strictly before any effect, both times in one unit
forks.EF-1: the four criteria make efficiencies cognizable; vagueness, the relevant market, nature-magnitude-likelihood and the monopoly clause condition crediting
forks.EDM-1: footnote 31's (b) decides merger specificity; (a) and (c) are reported
forks.TL-1: critical loss is the constant-cost breakeven L = Q s P / (P(1 + s) - C); a negative margin is NOTHING
forks.TL-2: recapture's 'exceed' and critical loss's 'less than' are strict
forks.TL-3: a SSNIP of zero percent or less is NOTHING

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Guidelines. An independent test pass (tests-independent.l4, 291 assertions, all satisfied) and an adversarial review were run on 2026-11-25 (NOTES.md sections 10 and 11); every finding was dealt with after the parent session's rulings of 2026-11-25, finding 3 by keeping the encoding's reading, and tests-independent.l4 carries a signature-only patch (NOTES.md section 10.1). One cross-reference (footnotes 87 and 90, 'n.81') was checked against the PDF; other quotations only against the deposited extraction. See NOTES.md sections 7, 9, 10 and 11.
